desc: Given an integer array nums that may contain negative numbers, and a positive integer k, return the length of the shortest non-empty contiguous subarray whose sum is at least k. If no such subarray exists, return -1.
hints: The classic shrinking window fails here because negative values mean that adding an element can lower the sum. Use prefix sums instead: you want the closest pair i < j with pre[j] - pre[i] ≥ k.
For a fixed j, a larger and closer i is always better. If pre[i1] ≥ pre[i2] with i1 > i2, then index i2 is useless.
Maintain a deque of indices with increasing prefix sums. At each j, pop from the front while pre[j] - pre[front] ≥ k (recording lengths), then pop from the back while pre[back] ≥ pre[j], then push j.
editorial: Let pre[0] = 0 and pre[j] = nums[0] + ... + nums[j-1]. We want the minimum j - i with i < j and pre[j] - pre[i] ≥ k.

Keep a deque of candidate start indices whose prefix sums are strictly increasing. When we reach j: (1) while the front index satisfies the condition, record j - front and pop it, since any later j would only give a longer length for that start; (2) while the back index has a prefix sum that is not smaller than pre[j], pop it, since j is a later and lower start that dominates it; (3) push j. Each index is pushed and popped once, so the algorithm runs in O(n) time and O(n) space.
